title: The Black Hole Era
description: After the protons, only black holes are left, slowly radiating. A black hole of a solar mass needs 10^67 years to evaporate, a supermassive one 10^100 - and then it ends in a flash. Unlocks the Last Flash of a Black Hole.

puzzle.goal: A black hole radiates as a black body at a temperature inversely proportional to its mass, so it loses mass at a rate dM/dt = −ħc⁴/(15360πG²M²) and gets brighter as it shrinks. Separate the variables and write the total time it needs to radiate away a mass M completely.
puzzle.name: Hawking evaporation time
puzzle.ask: The integral is 5120πG²M³/(ħc⁴). For a primordial black hole of M × 10¹⁰ kg (G in 10⁻¹¹, ħ in 10⁻³⁴, c in 10⁸ SI units), find its lifetime in thousands of years.
puzzle.method: dt = −dM/(dM/dt): put the mass-loss rate upside down and integrate from the full mass down to nothing.
